recollection

/rek-uh-LEK-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Recollection means the act or power of remembering, or a specific memory called back to mind.

Grandpa's recollection of the 1964 flood grew sharper as he walked us along the levee where it happened.

Worked Example

On the witness stand, Mrs. Alvarez admitted that her recollection of the getaway car had faded — she remembered the color clearly but could no longer picture the plates.

What's fading is her stored memory of a past event, called back under questioning. That remembered account — sharp in places, blurry in others — is a recollection.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

memory: Memory is the everyday, all-purpose word for something remembered, or for the power of remembering itself. Recollection is more deliberate and formal — the act of actively calling something back to mind, often under questioning. You simply have memories; a recollection is summoned.

remembrance: Remembrance is about honoring the past — ceremonies, keepsakes, moments of silence for what deserves to stay in mind. A recollection is just the memory itself, called back to mind for some practical purpose. Remembrance commemorates; a recollection merely reports what the mind retrieves.

reminiscence: A reminiscence is a fond, story-like memory shared aloud — the kind traded over dinner about old summers. A recollection is plainer and cooler: a memory called back to mind, with no warmth implied. Reminiscences entertain a table; recollections answer questions.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forgetfulness: the failure or inability to remember

oblivion: the state of being completely forgotten

Where it sits · how vividly the past returns — impression → recollection → flashback

impression vs. recollection: An impression is only a vague sense that something happened; a recollection brings back real detail.

flashback vs. recollection: A flashback is more intense than a recollection — the past floods back so vividly it feels like reliving it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again

Prefix — col-

Prefix — col-: together (a form of com-)

Root — -lect-

Root — -lect-: to gather, choose (Latin legere)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (again) + col- (together) + -lect- (gather): a recollection is literally what you gather back together in your mind — scattered details reassembled into a memory.

Use the root in a new word: eligible

Use the root in a new word: eligible: Only students who finish the safety course are eligible for the climbing trip — literally the ones who can be 'chosen out' of the group.

Root Check

Word Choice

Slightly formal

Memory is the everyday word; recollection sounds more deliberate and formal — the act of actively calling something back. The set phrase 'to have no recollection of' has a distinctly courtroom flavor, which is why witnesses and defendants use it so often.
